name: Art Nouveau Jewellery
summary: Jewels of the whiplash line. They show women, insects, orchids and dragonflies in enamel, glass, horn and opal. The design counts for more than the price of the stones.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel is a work of art: the design, the enamel and the line count for more than the value of the diamonds.
design_principles: Draw the piece in one flowing, asymmetrical line that comes from a stem, a wave or a lock of hair.
Choose a subject from nature or from a woman's body: a dragonfly, an orchid, a poppy, a swan, a head with loose hair.
Use enamel in many thin layers, and use plique-a-jour with no back plate, so that light passes through the colour.
Mix precious and cheap materials by their look: horn, glass and opal beside gold and diamonds.
Keep diamonds small and use them as a point of light, not as the main form.
Set a large opal, a moonstone or a piece of carved glass at the centre of the piece.
Make each piece a unique work and sign it on the front or the back.
Hang a pendant on a fine chain so that the piece moves with the body.
anti_patterns: Rows of equal stones in a symmetrical frame
Large bright diamonds as the main form

silhouette.shape: A large, flowing piece: a dragonfly corsage ornament, a pendant with a woman's head, or a hair comb with a spray of leaves.
silhouette.line: A whiplash curve, asymmetrical and organic, with long stems and wings and no straight edge.
silhouette.fit: Pinned at the corsage, hung on a long chain, or set in the hair as a comb.
silhouette.proportion: A corsage ornament is 8 to 15 cm wide; a pendant is 5 to 9 cm tall; a comb is 10 to 15 cm tall.
rules: Let one curved line run through the whole piece.
Fit a plique-a-jour panel in each wing or leaf, inside a thin gold wire frame.
Carve a horn comb with a leaf or an insect in relief.
Set one large opal or a glass cabochon at the centre.

fabrics.rule: Choose a material for its look, not its price: enamel, horn and opal beside small diamonds in gold.

methods: plique-a-jour enamel in a gold wire cell
layers of translucent enamel on gold
carved horn with a gold mount
small diamonds set as points of light
hand engraving and chasing of the gold
a single carved glass or opal as the centre stone
construction.closures: A pin with a safety catch on a brooch; a wire loop and a chain on a pendant; teeth on a comb.
construction.details: A woman's head, an insect with open wings, a spray of orchid or poppy, a long drop at the base and a signed back.

surface.pattern: Flowing stems, wings and hair; no repeat and no straight border.
surface.gloss: High on enamel and gold, 70 to 95 GU; horn and opal give a soft, deep glow.
surface.wear: Plique-a-jour enamel is thin and breaks if knocked; horn dries and cracks if kept in heat.

palette.strategy: Soft greens, blues and pinks in translucent enamel, set against yellow gold and the milky fire of opal.

making.scale: Unique pieces for rich patrons by a few Paris and Brussels workshops; many cheaper copies in silver and glass.
making.signs: A signed back, thin translucent enamel, an asymmetrical form and a mix of horn, glass and gold.

emotion.target_response: A dreamlike, sensual feeling: the viewer sees a living creature caught in glass and gold.

use_cases: a museum label for a Lalique-style piece
costume design for a belle epoque drama
an image prompt for a fin de siecle jewel
avoid_when: the brief wants strict symmetry or a geometric line
the brief wants platinum and a white, cold look

modifiers.how: Straighten each curve into a line and an angle, replace enamel with white stones and black onyx, and keep the fine work.
Replace plique-a-jour with hammered silver, remove the woman and the insect, and use cabochon stones.

ornament_level.note: The whiplash line carries the ornament; a pure line piece sits at the low end.
